documents.title: Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome
Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome
Un-Audited Financials Results For The Quarter Ended On 30Th June 2026

analysis.summary: Bhagyanagar India Limited released its Q1 FY27 investor presentation highlighting operational parameters, segment-wise revenues, and a composite scheme of arrangement involving the amalgamation of BCPL and demerger of the copper business into Tieramet Ltd. The company reported a Q1 FY27 revenue from operations of Rs. 70,507.54 lakhs and PAT of Rs. 2,024.52 lakhs. Management also detailed a preferential fund raise of Rs.

guidance.claim: The company aims to reach 5,000 crores in the year 2030.
guidance.quote: Our top line projection, as in earlier, this thing, has been project... we are aiming for 3,000 crores in the year 2030. That is, in 3 years, we are planning to reach 5,000 crores in the year 2030.

guidance.claim: Management targets a CAGR of between 20% to 25% for the next 3 to 4 years.
guidance.quote: 25% CAGR is our target for the next 3 to 4 years.

guidance.claim: The company expects a minimum volume growth of 15% to 20% every year.
guidance.quote: Between 15% to 20% should be our volume growth minimum every year.

guidance.claim: Management is hopeful of maintaining a 5% EBITDA margin throughout the next year.
guidance.quote: We are hopeful of maintaining 5% EBITDA margin throughout the next year, and on an increased top line.

guidance.claim: The company plans to increase value-added products up to 66% by the end of next year.
guidance.quote: So, we've already reached around 62% at the end of quarter four, and we are planning to get this up to 66% by the end of next year.

demand_outlook.claim: Management noted that growing sustainability focus and supply constraints are accelerating the transition from primary to recycled copper in India.
demand_outlook.quote: Growing sustainability focus and supply constraints are accelerating the transition from primary to recycled copper in India.

demand_outlook.claim: India is expected to become the second largest copper-consuming economy.
demand_outlook.quote: India is expected to become the second largest copper-consuming economy.

demand_outlook.claim: Global copper consumption is predicted to reach 50 million tonnes by 2050.
demand_outlook.quote: The world consumed around 26 million tonne of copper, which is predicted to become 50 million tonne by 2050, so this is almost doubling.

demand_outlook.claim: Growth in copper consumption will mainly be driven by EV and automotive, power and electrification, and renewable energy sectors.
demand_outlook.quote: This growth will mainly be driven by three sectors, EV and automotive. Because, EV requires a lot more copper than regular cars, power and electrification is also a big growth factor, and renewable energy.

demand_outlook.claim: Sourcing of copper scrap from the Gulf has experienced short-term disruptions and dried up.
demand_outlook.quote: The scrap coming from Gulf, which is of a short duration, short lead time material, has suddenly dried up.

demand_outlook.claim: Management noted that the overall copper demand in India has witnessed significant growth.
demand_outlook.quote: The overall copper demand in India has witnessed significant growth

capex_expansion.claim: The company has proposed a capex of 40 crores in the next 2 years.
capex_expansion.quote: We are proposing about 40 crores capex in the next 2 years.

capex_expansion.claim: Capacity reached 35,000 metric tonnes this year with the new 60-acre integrated facility near Hyderabad.
capex_expansion.quote: Our capacity has now reached 35,000 metric tonne this year, with the new, 60-acre integrated facility near Hyderabad.

margins_costs.claim: The company achieved an operational EBITDA margin of 46% and a PAT margin of 2.1% in its financial summary.
margins_costs.quote: Our operational EBITDA margin is 46%, our PAT margin is 2.1%, and our PE ratio is 17.71%.

margins_costs.claim: The company's EBITDA per kg for the year is around 43 rupees.
margins_costs.quote: Our EBITDA per kg for the year is around 43 rupees, which is very high compared to our peers, and as you can see, over the four quarters, our EBITDA per kg has been trending upwards.

margins_costs.claim: In quarter four, the company achieved an EBITDA per kg of around 62 rupees.
margins_costs.quote: With the quarter four, we achieved around 62 rupees per kg.

margins_costs.claim: Silver and tin-bearing bus bars give the company roughly about 10% EBITDA margins.
margins_costs.quote: So, we are, this product will give us roughly about 10%, EBITDA margins.

margins_costs.claim: Management highlighted a diversified copper products portfolio with an increasing focus on high-margin value-added products, driving margin expansion and differentiation.
margins_costs.quote: Diversified copper products portfolio with increasing focus on high-margin value-added products, driving margin expansion and differentiation

orders_capacity.claim: Copper sales volume increased by 34% from 18,000 metric tonnes to 24,000 metric tonnes.
orders_capacity.quote: Last year, we did around 18,000 metric tonne of volume of copper sales. Which has gone up by 34% to, 2 24,000 metric tonne.

orders_capacity.claim: The company has 500-plus clients with enduring relationships of over 30 years.
orders_capacity.quote: We have 500-plus clients with enduring relationships of over 30 years.

capital_allocation.claim: Total equity increased from retained earnings without any dilution.
capital_allocation.quote: And this increase in equity was not done through dilution, this was all done through retained earnings.

capital_allocation.claim: Working capital increased from 157 crores to 230 crores proportionally to revenue.
capital_allocation.quote: So, our working capital has gone up from 157 crores to 230 crores. And this increase in working capital is proportional to our revenue, so there's no, no reason to be concerned.

capital_allocation.claim: Management is looking at a fundraise of roughly about 150 crores.
capital_allocation.quote: So, we are looking at a fundraise. We are still not, come up with a final proposal, but we are looking at a fundraise of roughly about 150 crores.

risks_headwinds.claim: Shipping lines have been diverted, causing delays in raw material scrap logistics.
risks_headwinds.quote: And, the material which is coming from the rest of the world, the shipping lines have been diverted because a lot of shipping lines have a transit point in Dubai or somewhere in the Gulf before coming to India. That has got delayed.

management_commitments.claim: The government mandated that all new products made from non-ferrous metals must contain a minimum of 5% recycled content starting from FY28.
management_commitments.quote: Government has mandated that all new products made from non-ferrous metals must contain a minimum of 5% recycled content (starting from FY28)

management_commitments.claim: The company is planning to reach 5,000 crores in the year 2030.
management_commitments.quote: That is, in 3 years, we are planning to reach 5,000 crores in the year 2030.

management_commitments.claim: Management targets a 25% CAGR for the next 3 to 4 years.
management_commitments.quote: 25% CAGR is our target for the next 3 to 4 years.

management_commitments.claim: The company has proposed 40 crores capex in the next 2 years.
management_commitments.quote: We are proposing about 40 crores capex in the next 2 years.

management_commitments.claim: The company plans to increase value-added products up to 66% by the end of next year.
management_commitments.quote: we are planning to get this up to 66% by the end of next year.

management_commitments.claim: Management hopes to execute a fundraise of roughly about 150 crores in this financial year.
management_commitments.quote: We hope to do it in this financial year, definitely.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
